fight: Can a code/LLM be made to EXPRESS discriminative confidence, or is the verbalized interface fundamentally hopeless?

side_a.position: Verbalized confidence is a dead end: unstable across paraphrases/resamples, adversarially brittle, and encoded orthogonally to the true calibration direction in activation space.
claims: CSR: verbalized confidence unstable across paraphrases, abandon it for semantic-level reward
Miao&Ungar: calibration and verbal-confidence directions are orthogonal in activations; CoT contaminates the verbal direction
Obadinma: verbal confidence adversarially brittle
Our paper: self-verbal AUROC 0.52-0.56, 67% at max confidence; SFT gives calibration WITHOUT discrimination

side_b.position: TRAINED verbalized confidence IS discriminative — the failure is untrained self-report, not the interface. Distilling self-consistency/execution signal into stated confidence works.
claims: Rewarding Doubt: RL log-score reward => verbal AUROC 0.859, more discriminative than a trained probe, single A40 LoRA
Jang: SFT on self-consistency scalar => AUROC 50.57->81.25 on GSM8K
Uncertainty Distillation: MC-sample+isotonic+SFT into verbal bins => AUROC 0.69-0.79
ORCE: Spearman-rank DPO vs sampling surrogate => ECE 0.17->0.025
ConfTuner: proper tokenized Brier => +14.4% AUROC

evidence_quality_delta: Both empirical. Side B has more independent demonstrations (5+ methods, AUROC 0.79-0.86) but ALL on QA/math; side A's strongest point (orthogonality, instability) is mechanistic and also QA. Neither side has CODE evidence — the decisive gap.
scope_overlap: Genuine disagreement about the interface's ceiling, but both are QA-scoped. On code specifically it is UNRESOLVED — which is the paper's opening.

fight: Does verbal confidence for code fail (AUROC ~0.52) or succeed (AUROC 0.75-0.97)?

side_a.position: Verbal confidence for code barely beats random.
claims: Our paper: verbal AUROC 0.519-0.564 on HumanEval (self-assessment, same model rates own solution)
Functional Entropy: verbalized confidence inconsistent 0.52-0.80

side_b.position: External LLM-as-judge verbalized confidence discriminates well on simple code.
claims: AutoProbe: external LLM-as-Judge verbalized confidence 0.75-0.97 accuracy on independent-unit code (beats internal probing), collapses to 0.70-0.80 on repo-level

evidence_quality_delta: Both empirical. Reconciliation likely: SELF-assessment (own solution, in-context) fails; EXTERNAL/fresh-context judge succeeds; and complexity mediates (simple vs repo-level reverse the ranking).
scope_overlap: Scoped differently (self vs external judge; unit vs repo) and probably both right — the reconciliation IS a finding.

fight: Can a cheap single-pass interface (probe/logit) ever match the expensive n-sample oracle for code?

side_a.position: No — single-pass hidden states hit an informational ceiling for code correctness.
claims: AutoProbe/Openia: single-pass probes plateau 0.63-0.79; oracle upper bound ~0.66-0.77 on short code
Sharma&David: log-probs NOT significantly correlated with correctness on LiveCodeBench; only symbolic-execution clustering restores signal
Our paper: log-prob AUROC 0.668; post-hoc calibration DEGRADES AUROC

side_b.position: Yes — trained single-pass modules recover most of the multi-sample signal (in QA).
claims: Semantic Entropy Probes: single-generation hidden-state probe approximates semantic entropy at ~0 overhead
Dist2ill: one-pass module approximates sampling-derived confidence
Sample-scaling: n=2 hybrid gives +12 AUROC then diminishes

evidence_quality_delta: Side A code-specific and includes an oracle-bound argument (strong). Side B is QA and never validated on code. For CODE, side A currently wins => 'probe recovers oracle' is a risky headline.
scope_overlap: Genuine on code; side B's success is out-of-domain (QA). The code informational ceiling is a real constraint.

fight: Is the calibration disconnect a real signal or a metric/benchmark artifact?

side_a.position: ECE and near-perfect AUROC may be artifacts: ECE_bin is biased, protocol-sensitive, and HumanEval is contaminated.
claims: Roelofs: ECE_bin biased, equal-width worst; debiased estimators change conclusions
Kim&Kang: prob-vs-verbal ECE gap flips sign with conditioning
Riddell/TRACER: HumanEval/MBPP overlap pretraining incl. semantic 'shared-logic' contamination
Spiess: Platt 'bucket collapse' fakes ECE~0 while Skill Score shows no utility

side_b.position: The discrimination gap is robust: it shows up on AUROC (binning-free), across models, and via execution ground-truth.
claims: Our paper: sampling AUROC 0.987 with INDEPENDENT labels; verbal 0.52 — a rank-metric gap immune to ECE binning
ConSelf: replicates difficulty-level disconnect on same models + LiveCodeBench (contamination-resistant)

evidence_quality_delta: Side A raises valid threats to ECE-based claims; side B's AUROC + LiveCodeBench replication answers them. Net: paper must use AUROC-primary + a contamination-free benchmark to be bulletproof.
scope_overlap: Genuine methodological caution; resolvable by design (rank metrics + LiveCodeBench).

fight: Can accuracy and calibration be optimized jointly in one training objective?

side_a.position: No — there is a proven gradient conflict.
claims: DCPO: theoretically proves gradient conflict between jointly optimizing accuracy and a calibration term in one reward

side_b.position: Yes with the right surrogate — discrimination-first/proper-scoring losses preserve accuracy.
claims: CAPO: AUC/discrimination-first surrogate preserves accuracy
Beyond Binary Rewards: bounded proper scoring rule yields accurate+calibrated policy
Rewarding Doubt: negligible accuracy impact

evidence_quality_delta: Side A theoretical (narrow conditions); side B empirical with multiple existence proofs. Design implication: decouple or use proper-scoring/advantage-reshaping, don't naively add an ECE penalty.
scope_overlap: Both right under different objective designs; a design caveat, not a blocker.
